text: Memorypalace. Revisit the moments you almost forgot. A personal memory companion that links changes in EEG activity with recorded context. Begin the 36-second film on the next slide.

Play the embedded 36-second concept film with sound. It illustrates the intended wearable experience, using the approved mannequin and revised desk reaction. The neural strengths shown in the film are illustrative story values. The running prototype uses the phone camera and supports synthetic EEG replay plus a Crown adapter.

text: The near miss, the database incident and the unfamiliar word are narrative examples, not clinical detections. The problem is the lost context and the effort of reviewing a whole day. Memorypalace aims to make a small collection of meaningful moments easy to revisit.

text: Hardware concept: Neurosity Crown for sensing EEG and Ray-Ban Meta glasses for first-person context, supported by the Memorypalace app. Crown is an EEG sensor, not a neurostimulation device; Ray-Ban Meta glasses are not Meta Quest. The current working recorder is an Android phone camera, with a Crown stream adapter. Twenty minutes is the requested onboarding target, not a measured result; code baseline currently uses 120 seconds. Sources: hardware-demo/eegdemo/pipeline.py; hardware-demo/README.md; https://neurosity.co/crown ; https://wearables.developer.meta.com/docs/develop/dat/build-integration-android/

text: Current implementation: clean frontal EEG, theta (4–8 Hz) over alpha (8–13 Hz) band power, four-second non-overlapping windows, per-wearer z-score, threshold 2.0, four consecutive elevated windows. It measures a sustained load proxy. Phase-shift detection is not present in the inspected implementation; avoid describing this method as phase-shift inference or as a state-of-the-art benchmark. Source: confusion-detector/src/config.py; confusion-detector/src/cognitive_load.py; hardware-demo/eegdemo/pipeline.py.

text: Illustrative arithmetic: raw theta/alpha index 3.0; A mean 1.0 and standard deviation 0.5 gives z=4.0; B mean 2.6 and standard deviation 0.5 gives z=0.8. These are explanatory values, not measured people or clinical thresholds. The implemented trigger threshold is z=2.0. Source: confusion-detector/src/detector.py and config.py. The chart remains editable beneath its animated video overlay.

text: Four consecutive windows above z=2.0 are required. No overlap means samples are not reused; it does not prove statistical independence of brain activity. The active backend finalizes an ongoing recording on this trigger, attaches the signal context, and saves it. The concept film illustrates the broader event-capture vision. Sources: confusion-detector/src/config.py; hardware-demo/eegdemo/server.py Runtime.trigger.

text: Controlled comparison reported in confusion-detector/README.md, The one result that matters: 4-second windows, 75% overlap (hop 1s) 30.3 false alarms/hour; 50% overlap (hop 2s) 18.9; no overlap (hop 4s) 1.3. Same stationary synthetic fixture and threshold. Do not generalize the absolute rate to people or drifting baselines; the drifting fixture reported 7.2/hour at the default setting. This chart is engineering evidence for avoiding repeated samples, not a clinical performance claim.

text: Sponsor challenge is quoted from DOCS_sponsor/meta: Bringing People Closer Together with AI. Implemented Share flow: user selects moments and recipient, Muse Spark writes a grounded first-person note, user reviews and edits, then invokes native Share or Copy. This deck does not send anything. Meta also powers scene descriptions, voice transcription and Memory Guard when selected. Sources: app/components/share/SharePage.tsx; hardware-demo/eegdemo/agent.py share_note; hardware-demo/eegdemo/server.py compose_share. Logo: official Meta logo via Wikimedia Commons, https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/ab/Meta-Logo.png ; brand source https://www.meta.com/brand/resources/meta/company-brand/ .

text: Challenge source: DOCS_sponsor/VoloRidge. Dataset: OpenNeuro ds006394 / NEMAR on006394, surprise-related visual and auditory events, CC0; 33 participants listed, 56 usable recordings. This is offline leave-one-subject-out logistic regression, not a live Memorypalace accuracy claim. Values from xueqi-validation/results/electrode_ablation_table.csv: 16 channels AUC .712, 8 .705, 4 .697, 2 temple .599. Channel positions differ across configurations, so the chart does not isolate channel count alone. Source: xueqi-validation/RESULTS.md. https://openneuro.org/datasets/ds006394 ; logo from https://www.voloridge.com/themes/custom/voloridge/logo.svg .

text: Actual wiring: Crown publisher sends EEG to Python backend. Android camera client polls authenticated commands and uploads video to the backend. Backend persists the catalog, calls Meta enrichment and Elastic indexing. Next.js browser accesses backend through server routes. Source: hardware-demo/eegdemo/server.py; pipeline.py; library.py; elastic_store.py; app/lib/backend.ts. The native diagram is editable.
